transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-08-19
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM), Maya (Orion Dir. ML), Liam (Eng Mgr), Sofia (Data Sci), Noah (DevOps)

Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Reviewed latest benchmark runs across candidate models (redwood-codex-v1, gpt-like-open-1, redwood-quant-small).
- Discussed pinning strategy: pin to redwood-codex-v1-2026-07 then gradual rollout with fallback to quantized variant; plan for quick rollback on quality regressions.
- Action items: share updated benchmarks, prepare pinning config, provide user queries for latency tests, check VPC network for private tests.

00:00 Alex Martinez: "All right, hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check in — um — we'll go through the benchmark numbers first, then model pinning proposal, and then next steps. Priya, you want to start with the results?"

00:42 Priya Shah: "Yeah, sure. So we ran the three key workloads this week — intent classification, multi-turn summarization, and the search-rewrite pipeline. The headline: redwood-codex-v1 (the non-quantized) is still best-in-class for quality, p95 latency around 220ms for short prompts on our test fleet, p99 about 480ms for the 1K sequence tests. The quantized variant (redwood-quant-small) drops median latency by ~30% but we saw small regressions on several summarization prompts, like hallucinations increasing a hair on longer contexts."

02:10 Liam O'Connor: "When you say 'a hair', can you give examples? That was our worry — tradeoff between latency and factuality."

02:35 Priya Shah: "Right. e.g., the product detail summarization on longer SKU pages — the quant model sometimes drops company-specific terms. It's borderline, but for customer-facing messaging we observed a 4-6% drop in exact-entity recall. For internal intents it's fine. Also worth noting the KV cache warms differently; the quantized variant has a slightly different attention kernel so cache hit behavior varied."

04:05 Maya Chen: "So for our use-case — order status and returns triage — entity recall is important. We could tolerate a small latency bump if it buys quality. What's the cost delta?"

04:30 Priya Shah: "Token-level cost for redwood-codex-v1 is approximately 1.0x baseline; the quant-small is about 0.62x in our runs due to lower GPU utilization and faster kernels. But because codex has higher hit-rate with caching it may amortize in some scenarios. Alex, I think you have the cost spreadsheet?"

05:10 Alex Martinez: "Yeah I sent an earlier sheet, but I'll upload the updated benchmark with per-route cost, p95/p99, and the sample outputs. Expect that in the next few hours. Quick note — pricing we show for hosted vs dedicated will change unit economics; if you go dedicated and pin a model, you'd get more consistent latency but a higher commitment."

06:22 Noah Patel: "On the infra side, we tested peering to Redwood Private last night; the VPC peering worked but there was an egress rule that blocked some monitoring endpoints. I'll re-open the rule and rerun the test. For on-prem we still need the runbook — the playbook for rollback and failover."

07:15 Jordan Lee: "We can share our rollback playbook template; Priya will adapt it to the model pin/fallback flow. Important: we recommend a staged rollout — 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic fallback if quality regressions exceed thresholds or latency SLOs breach for >5 minutes."

08:02 Sofia Alvarez: "How do you detect 'quality regressions' automatically? Is that tied to our labeled eval set or can we do live quality sampling?"

08:35 Priya Shah: "Good question. We usually do a hybrid: run continuous evals on a labeled prompt set for regression detection (precision/recall/ROUGE where relevant) and a small realtime human-sampled check for production signals. For the POC, we recommend starting with your labeled set (the 2k prompts you mentioned last week) and then add a 1% live sampling with quick annotator feedback."

10:11 Liam O'Connor: "Is there an API/console hook to automate the rollback on regression? We don't want manual intervention at 3am."

10:27 Priya Shah: "Yes — Redwood has route-level rollouts and automatic fallback policies. You can define thresholds (e.g., quality score drop > 3 points or p95 > 800ms) to trigger immediate routing to a fallback model, and an optional page to on-call. The only caveat is that the quality score requires your labeled eval metrics to be pushed into Redwood Optimize or our eval webhook."

12:05 Maya Chen: "SSO and audit logs — we need SOC2-friendly logs of which model versions served which request. Is that available in the Private deployment?"

12:30 Alex Martinez: "Yes, Private includes request-level audit logs and model-version metadata. You can query by model version and get token counts and request IDs. We also integrate with KMS for key management. We'll include a sample of the audit export in the security pack we send."

13:40 Noah Patel: "And what about data retention? We have to keep logs for 12 months for compliance."

13:55 Jordan Lee: "We can configure retention per customer in Private. For hosted we have standard retention; for enterprise we can negotiate longer retention windows and ship logs to your SIEM via S3/Kinesis."

15:20 Sofia Alvarez: "Back to pinning: what's the proposed pinned version? You mentioned redwood-codex-v1-2026-07?"

15:35 Priya Shah: "Yes, the recommendation is to pin to redwood-codex-v1-2026-07 as the primary for the POC because it maximizes accuracy for summarization and entity recall. Then set the fallback to redwood-quant-small-2026-08 which is faster and cheaper; fallback triggers on either quality drop or latency/p95 SLO breach. We'll also keep an earlier stable tag in case we need immediate rollback (e.g., redwood-codex-v1-2026-05)."

17:02 Liam O'Connor: "If we pin to the 2026-07 build, how do we get patch updates/critical fixes? Will we have to repin?"

17:20 Priya Shah: "Patch updates are handled by the model lifecycle policy. We can do minor patches in-place if they are backward compatible, or you can require explicit repin for any patch. For the POC we recommend manual repin so you can validate outputs on the labeled set before going 100%."

18:45 Maya Chen: "What about canary traffic? We want to test the quant model on 10% of sessions first but ensure weighted users are balanced across geos."

19:05 Alex Martinez: "Redwood's routing supports percent-based rollouts and region-aware routing. You can route based on geo or customer segment. We'll include an example config for 10% canary in the repo."

20:30 Sofia Alvarez: "One gotcha we saw: some of our longer queries with product tables caused tokenization differences and affected the p99. Did you tune sequence length and compaction?"

21:00 Priya Shah: "We adjusted the tokenizer truncation and prefix caching; caching behavior improved p95 but p99 still spikes on worst-case long docs. We suggested batching small queries while isolating long-context requests to dedicated queues to avoid head-of-line blocking."

22:48 Noah Patel: "Does that require separate hardware pools?"

23:05 Priya Shah: "Usually you can specify route->capacity profile. On Dedicated you can reserve a GPU pool for long-context workloads; on hosted we emulate via priority queues but dedicated gives better isolation."

24:40 Liam O'Connor: "Cost-wise, if we reserve a dedicated pool for long contexts, what's the expected uplift?"

25:00 Alex Martinez: "Roughly +20-30% for dedicated reserved capacity for the high-memory instances depending on utilization. We'll quantify in the updated cost sheet. Remember, dedicated reduces variability which might be worthwhile if p99 is a hard SLO."

27:15 Maya Chen: "Let's talk about monitoring. We want token-level cost, per-route p95/p99, and alerts on quality regression. Can Redwood do that in the console?"

27:40 Jordan Lee: "Yes — Redwood Console has per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, tracing hooks, and alerting tied to evals. We can set up out-of-the-box dashboards for your key intents and add custom metrics from your labeled evals."

29:02 Sofia Alvarez: "One more item — model explainability. Some product folks want to know why the model made a particular rewrite. Any feature for structured output or provenance?"

29:28 Priya Shah: "We support structured response modes and function/tool calling; you can force JSON-schema outputs or include provenance fields if you run inference with tracing enabled. There's a cost for tracing heavier payloads but it helps debug."

31:10 Liam O'Connor: "Okay, I'd like to nail down the pin + fallback flow in writing. Can we get a sample YAML config?"

31:28 Priya Shah: "Yes — I'll produce a sample pinning YAML: primary: redwood-codex-v1-2026-07; fallback: redwood-quant-small-2026-08; rollout: 10/50/100; auto-fallback thresholds: quality_drop>3, p95>800ms for >5m; tie to eval webhook. I'll add it to the repo and send to you."

33:05 Maya Chen: "And the rollback playbook?"

33:15 Jordan Lee: "We'll attach our standard rollback runbook. Short version: monitor evals for 10 minutes post-rollout, if threshold tripped — automatic rollback to previous pinned version and notify oncall; follow up with root cause and new repin proposal."

34:40 Sofia Alvarez: "Testing cadence — we want nightly batch runs of the 2k labeled set plus a weekly full-run of the 10k holdout set. Is that feasible?"

35:00 Priya Shah: "Yes, we can schedule nightly evals; the full weekly run is fine but we recommend doing it off-peak hours to avoid heavy cost."

36:20 Noah Patel: "From ops: we need a checklist to validate network, certs, and perf before the dedicated pilot. I'll own that checklist and share dates."

36:45 Alex Martinez: "Great. To recap, recommended pin: redwood-codex-v1-2026-07; fallback redwood-quant-small-2026-08; staged rollout with automated fallback; Priya to deliver YAML and rollback playbook; Alex to share updated cost/benchmark sheet; customer to provide queries and validate retention/VPC."

38:10 Maya Chen: "That works for us. If we validate within the next two weeks we can go to a limited pilot by early September."

39:00 Liam O'Connor: "One more quick question on latency SLOs — what's the expected improvement if we tune batching and caching further?"

39:20 Priya Shah: "We saw another ~10-15% improvement on median with optimized batching and prefix caching after the last tuning pass; p99 improvements are smaller but more consistent with dedicated capacity. We'll include a tuning checklist in the doc."

40:12 Alex Martinez: "Okay, we'll follow up with the artifacts. Anything else?"

40:25 Sofia Alvarez: "Nope — thanks everyone."

40:30 Jordan Lee: "Thanks all, we'll send notes and action items."

End of meeting

References/attachments mentioned: cost_benchmarks_2026-08-19.xlsx (link sent in chat), model-pinning-sample.yaml (to be uploaded), security-pack.zip (SOC2 + audit log examples), rollback-playbook-template.pdf (shared)

Recap (auto): Primary pin redwood-codex-v1-2026-07; fallback redwood-quant-small-2026-08; staged rollout 10/50/100; action items assigned; files to be shared by Redwood this week.
